previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted with persistent left lower quadrant abdominal pain and diarrhea following incomplete recovery from a recent episode of C. difficile colitis. Despite initial treatment with vancomycin and metronidazole at an outside hospital, he remained symptomatic and unable to tolerate oral intake. Laboratory evaluation revealed mild hyponatremia, which improved with IV fluids and albumin. He was continued on oral vancomycin, with gradual symptom improvement over four days. His liver function remained stable, and home diuretics were resumed as his hydration status improved. He tolerated a regular diet, had no further vomiting or significant diarrhea, and was discharged home on a 7-week tapered course of vancomycin and a 9-week course of Saccharomyces boulardii. Follow-up was arranged with primary care, infectious disease, and hepatology.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL INDICATION: ___ man with cirrhosis and hepatocellular
carcinoma status post radiofrequency ablation and TACE, selective
chemoembolization for reccurent lesion.
 
PHYSICIANS: Dr ___ ( Fellow) and Dr. ___ (Attending
radiologist) performed the procedure. Dr. ___ was present and supervised
throughout the procedure. 
 
PROCEDURES:
1. Celiac arteriogram.
2. Selective left hepatic artery catheterization and rotational angiography
with Dyna CT reconstruction.
3. Selective LHA third-order branch catheterization. 
3. Selective chemoembolization of the segment II of the left hepatic lobe.
4. Right external iliac artery sheath injection and Angioseal closure.
 
INTRAVENOUS MEDICATIONS ADMINISTERED DURING THE PROCEDURE: The procedure was
performed under monitored conscious sedation. The patient received a total
quantity of 100 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of Versed during the total procedural
time of 115 minutes, while his hemodynamic parameters and pulse oximetry were
continuously monitored by a trained radiology nurse.
 
INTRA-ARTERIAL MEDICATIONS ADMINISTERED DURING THE PROCEDURE: 30 mg of
doxorubicin, 4 mL lipiodol, 5 mL of 1% lidocaine.
 
Informed consent for the procedure was obtained from the patient via
professional interpreter after risks and potential complications of the
procedure had been explained. The skin of the right inguinal region was
prepped and draped in sterile fashion. Usual timeout and huddle protocols were
carried out prior to the procedure according to the ___ policy. 

Under fluoroscopic guidance and palpation, right common femoral artery was
localized superficial to the anatomical landmark of the right femoral head.
Local anesthesia was affected by 1% lidocaine. Right common femoral artery was
accessed using a single wall micropuncture technique, utilizing 21-gauge
needle. A 5 ___ sheath was advanced into the right common femoral artery
over 0.035 ___ guidewire. A 5 ___ ___ catheter was then advanced
beyond the illiac bifurcation and formed followed by selective catheterization
of the celiac
artery. 
 
___ renegade microcatheter was advanced through the ___ catheter
successfully into the left hepatic artery and then further advanced under
direct fluoroscopic guidance into the third-order branch of the left hepatic
artery supplying the target lesion. A Transcend wire and
double-angle microglide wire were used in conjunction with Renegade
microcatheter. Once location of the microcatheter was documented by
flouroscopy to provide the blood supply for the targeted lesion,
chemoembolization was successfully delivered under continued fluoroscopic
visualization.
 
A dyna CT was performed which demonstrated a paucity of the chemo in one of
the targeted area. The renegade catheter was pulled back and chemo followed by
100 - 300 micron embospheres were delivered.

Angio seal was deployed and manual compression was applied to hemostasis.
 
FINDINGS:
1. Again seen is variant anatomy in the celiac and SMA distributions with a
replaced left hepatic artery originating from the left gastric artery, and a
replaced right hepatic artery arising from the SMA.  
2. Falciform artery was visualized on DynaCT arising from a branch of the left
hepatic artery.
3.  TACE to the left lobe targeting the nodule seen on prior cross-sectional
imaging.
 
CONCLUSION: Successful selective chemoembolization of the segment II lesion
supplied by the left hepatic artery.

The treated lesion is located along the posterior margin of the area of
Ethiodol uptake (2:13).  Some foci of high density Ethiodol within the lateral
portion of the lesion are residua of a previous TACE.  There has been prior
cholecystectomy.  There is no evidence of non-targeted embolization.  A
cluster of high density structures in the lower abdomen are unchanged from
prior studies and likely represent dropped gallstones (2:56).  Hypodense

shows a nodular contour consistent with known cirrhosis.  Splenomegaly is
unchanged.  The non-contrast appearance of the pancreas, bilateral adrenal
glands, and kidneys is unremarkable.  Multiple varices are seen in the left
upper quadrant and there has been recanalization of the paraumbilical vein. 
Abdominal loops of large and small bowel appear within normal limits.  Changes
of gynecomastia are noted.  The tiny fluid collection in the gallbladder fossa
adjacent to the surgical clips is stable in size measuring 1.2 x 1.9 cm.

BONE WINDOWS:  There is multilevel degenerative change of the thoracic spine
and lumbar spine.  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions are
identified.

consistent with post-TACE changes.  The region of Ethiodol uptake includes the
